Re: Hardin — I don't think he's actually anomalous. Rather, he's a case of incredibly advanced technology that the Foundation has yet to fully replicate (there's a subtle distinction there, I realize).

Xiaoshan is (partly) fronting. I based her off my father (a Marine). She pretends to be invulnerable, because the men and women under her command need her to be invulnerable. She's also just been dealing with SCP-072 for far too long — he has a way of deforming your sense of scale.

That being said, you're not the first person to point out that Xiaoshan comes off as over-the-top. I might have over-sold it, or at least not given enough sense that she's fronting — the introduction is intended to do that, but it happened ten years ago. Either way, I appreciate the comment!

That was an interesting story, but I have some issues, here.

First and foremost, I think you really, really should take some time to explain Hardin in the tale. As much as you have a perfectly sound explanation for his anomalies, and the Foundation not locking him up for them, this explanation is amiss in the tale, and that really left me with the impression of a Marty Stu with no reason whatsoever to be there.

It kind of lessened with time, he's a good character, but it doesn't seem credible for such an anomaly to be so casually working and even traveling through sites.

Second is a general dislike of several of the premises common to most of this canon, so they are not really something you should do anything about, but with the first thing it all weights enough for me to not vote for this. In this regard, Hardin is just a little too "good at almost everything", but Xiaoshan is over-the-top. Maybe not too over-the-top (that is Able, hands down), but over-the-top nonetheless, and she's a character that I really want to like.

I like the concept of a character "striking back, out of the painting", but wouldn't firing a gun in the air be like a flatlander firing a flat gun left? "Up" is still within the three spatial dimensions.

Pretty much. Hardin did some rough computations and figured out a way to angle the gun so he could fire the bullet slightly into the W plane (as opposed to the X, Y, and Z planes). Basically, when he fired "up", he was firing "up, and slightly to W+".

Think of it like abusing a floating point error: He figured out the precise degree to fire this gun so that the bullet would 'bleed' into the fourth axis. The bullet never hit the ceiling; it just shrank into an unseen point and popped out of view.

I merely had him fire it at the ceiling because I figured this would help ease the metaphor (of him firing 'up' out of the 'painting').

The reality bender exists in 4D (he's this guy), so our 3D world is to him as a 2D world is to us.

Think of our world as a 2D painting. Not just a 3D world flattened into a painting (with perspective); a world where perspective never existed. A world where every molecule that exists is represented in a single plane. As a 3D creature, I can look at this painting and see everything at once. I can see every bone in your body, every blood vessel, every muscle fiber, every wrinkle in your brain. I can even just reach over and grab those things. Move 'em around, smooth those wrinkles out — etc (hence the seizures).

That's how our world looks to the tessellated man: all our molecules are laid out for him on a single plane. Now, imagine you're looking at this "living painting", poking people's brains, having yourself a good time… and suddenly one of these flat 2D figures looks up out of the painting, right at you. He fires his gun out of the painting, and the bullet flies right past you.

That's what Hardin did to scare him off.

ETA: Here's an explanation from Carl Sagan re: Flatland, which helps explain the concept visually. Basically, we live in Flatland, and the 3D "apple" is the 4D tessellated man.

On the off-chance anyone wants to use Researcher Sebastian Hardin for anything, here's your basic fact sheet:

  • He's a cyborg, not an android (he gets irritable when people confuse the terms).
  • He's a huge sci-fi nerd and kind of a transhumanist.
  • His head's appearance is based on Salvius (an open source robot). He got it after an encounter with SCP-212.
  • He's modified his sensory array to allow him to perform short-range Van Eck phreaking.
  • He's a Computer Science major who previously worked for the Department of Analytics.
  • His coworkers in the DoA have a running betting pool on how he: 1) eats, 2) drinks, and 3) breathes.

AUTHOR NOTES
– hide block

This is a one-shot story intended to be in the resurrection canon, though it should be able to stand on its own.

  • The agent mentioned at the beginning (the one who talks to Xiaoshan) is intended to be an oblique reference to Lombardi.
  • The 'tessellated man' that attacks Area 25B is another oblique reference to Fishmonger's SCP-299 (4D man; no longer on the site).
  • If you're wondering where Hardin got his robot-head from, the answer can be found here.
  • Hardin is named after Salvor Hardin, the character from Asimov's Foundation series. Specifically, two quotes from Salvor exemplify him:
    • "Violence is the last refuge of the incompetent."
    • "Never let your sense of morals prevent you from doing what is right."
